slice: E2: executable vendor integer model boundary
observed: No executable vendor-model lane exists for emitted AArch64 integer instructions.
A non-check generate-target invocation rewrites every output even when bytes are unchanged, touching Cargo inputs and causing avoidable downstream rebuilds.

scope.included: A pinned, verbatim Arm ASL-to-Sail scalar integer slice, a bounded runtime using Sail-generated code, and differential execution of actual compiler-emitted straight-line instruction words against EvoIR, EvoMIR, native hardware and QEMU. Fix no-op target generation with write-if-different.
scope.domain: Nine operations add/sub/mul/and/or/xor/shl/lshr/ashr at source widths 1,2,8,16,31,32,33,63,64. ABI inputs/results are bits<64>; narrow operations use explicit truncate/extend. Shift counts are restricted to the source-defined range before execution. Exact-bit constant transport controls are separate.
scope.boundary: No memory, calls, inline assembly, FP/SIMD, privileged operations or full application model execution. Existing leaf-frame option is used only for these no-memory fixtures; do not strip prologues after emission. RET is an explicit harness termination boundary. Unknown instructions and out-of-domain features fail closed.
scope.unchanged: Production lowering, allocation, selection, interpreter semantics, existing option defaults, P0/g0/R03 and frozen timing results.
scope.glue: Reset and input/output glue is separate from verbatim vendor decode/execute/helper bodies. Unsupported instrumentation/state must fail if executed, not be replaced by successful no-op semantics.

source.origin: Automatically translated Arm 2023-03 ASL; preserve upstream license and exact source spans. A deterministic named selector records source/slice hashes. No handwritten ISA replacement.

sail.qualification: The model README tested 0.17.1. Qualify the pinned newer release explicitly; incompatibility is a recorded bounded integration result, never PASS.

qemu.transport: Freestanding ELF and semihosting; no VM disk.

corpus.input_rule: First eight pairs cover zero, one, all ones, sign edge and alternating bits; remaining 24 use a fixed documented xorshift64 generator. Map shift count modulo source width. Freeze concrete generated vectors with the implementation before acceptance.
corpus.claim: Exact bits, no tolerance. Count model/native/interpreter outcomes separately; unsupported cases are not passes.

sequence: Commit plan before imports or execution.
RED for no-op output mtime churn and absent model lane; fix generator without changing generated bytes.
Qualify pinned Sail executable in the existing sealed container, then select verbatim vendor dependencies and expose reset/word execution through narrow glue.
Use actual public EvoIR parse/execute, MIR lower/interpret/allocate/verify/emit APIs; run the frozen corpus through vendor runtime, native hardware and diskless QEMU.
Full workspace and focused tests; compare native and six-TU objects to retained E1 baselines; compact receipt and one-page note, retire temporary model build products.

acceptance.generator: Repeated public generation preserves both bytes and mtimes of all eight unchanged outputs; corrupt or missing output is repaired without rewriting others. Regeneration remains exact.
acceptance.runtime: Every admitted corpus case agrees bit-for-bit across all executed lanes, with unknown opcode and domain failures explicit. No handmade numeric reference stands in for the vendor lane.
acceptance.objects: Reuse E1 current migration baselines: 384 objects per OS and 24 six-TU A/B/profile objects, two-build identity and full-byte equality. No new optimization benefit.
acceptance.stop: Time-box initial tool/dependency qualification to 30 minutes of tool work. If no bounded original dependency slice is executable, record exact blocker and disposition, do not substitute invented semantics or build the full ISA; switch to remaining independent quality slices. SMT is a separately frozen E3 step.

resources.retention: One tool archive/cache and model capture only. No full disassembly, workspace clone, new kernel tree or VM disk. Retain small source slice, vectors, receipts and minimal reproducer; temporary generated C/objects removed after hashes/results. Current E1 objects remain protected until replaced.

claim_ceiling: A bounded integer vendor-model differential, not complete ISA/compiler correctness, memory/provenance/FP validation, full application/kernel acceptance, SMT proof or default optimization admission.
